title: Central Maui wastewater reclamation facility funding
summary: On Nov. 25, Bill 180 was introduced to add a $10.5 million state grant for the Central Maui Regional Wastewater Reclamation Facility in Waikapū. On Nov. 10 the commission voted six to support land use changes on about 14.9 acres, sending its recommendation and comments to the County Council. The plant, designed for 4 million gallons a day, is projected to start in late 2029 or later.

timeline.text: Bill 180 would add a $10.5 million state grant for the Central Maui Regional Wastewater Reclamation Facility in Waikapū.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: The motion passed with six yes votes.
timeline.body: Maui Planning Commission

timeline.text: Comments to be sent to the Council include designing the soil treatment system for maximum nitrogen removal.
timeline.body: Maui Planning Commission

timeline.text: Staff will send the Council the commission's recommendation along with commissioners' comments.
timeline.body: Maui Planning Commission

timeline.text: A commissioner moved to support the Planning Department's recommendation, which goes to the County Council.
timeline.body: Maui Planning Commission

timeline.text: A wastewater official said the new plant would take about 1.5 million of the 5.5 million gallons per day now going to the existing plant.
timeline.body: Maui Planning Commission

timeline.text: A second testifier supported the project.
timeline.body: Maui Planning Commission

timeline.text: One testifier asked the commission to delay action until several issues are resolved.
timeline.body: Maui Planning Commission

timeline.text: The project team said the requests go next to the Maui County Council, then construction permits and construction.
timeline.body: Maui Planning Commission

timeline.text: The plant is designed to treat up to 4 million gallons per day.
timeline.body: Maui Planning Commission

timeline.text: A soil aquifer treatment system will be the backup disposal system the health department requires.
timeline.body: Maui Planning Commission

timeline.text: All treated water is meant to be R1 recycled water, which the engineer called the highest quality.
timeline.body: Maui Planning Commission

timeline.text: The project team said the inland site protects against tsunamis, shoreline erosion and sea level rise.
timeline.body: Maui Planning Commission

timeline.text: The facility would add treatment capacity and make recycled water for farming and other non-drinking uses.
timeline.body: Maui Planning Commission

timeline.text: The county wants land use changes on about 14.9 acres to build a new Central Maui wastewater reclamation facility.
timeline.body: Maui Planning Commission

timeline.text: The director confirmed the 14.9-acre plant site does not need the Land Use Commission because it is under 15 acres.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The director said the county has environmental permits for the new plant and is working through land approvals.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The environmental management director said the new plant should be running before the school needs service in July 2031.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The new Central Maui wastewater plant is projected to begin operating in late 2029 or later.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The committee recommended the bill on first reading with nine ayes.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The wastewater project needs 7.13 percent of the parcel, or 14.9 of its 209 acres.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The open space fund is limited to land conservation, so it must be repaid for the part of the parcel used for wastewater.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The parcel was first bought with open space money for about $5.2 million.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The committee backed moving $372,933 from the Sewer Fund to the open space fund for land needed for the Central Maui Wastewater Facility.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The member withdrew the loan motion for now.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The member said the project is stalled while waiting on the County plant, and the community needs its affordable housing and school.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: A member said the Central Maui wastewater facility may not be working until 2031.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: A member proposed a $500,000 zero-interest loan to design a private wastewater plant for part of a country town development.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: Bill 30 adds $3.5 million for the Central Maui Regional Wastewater Reclamation Facility in Waikapū.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: The department said $10.5 million covers the design phase of the Central Maui facility.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: A wastewater official said the department will need the council's help with a community plan amendment and a zoning change for the facility.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: Design of the Central Maui Wastewater Reclamation Facility is 60% done and on schedule.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The committee reviewed the status of the Central Maui Wastewater Reclamation Facility and R1 recycled water expansion in West and South Maui.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: Bill 30 passed seven to two on a separate roll call vote.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting
